# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1458
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1458
- **Title**: feat(1380): total recall for giant sessions — ledger pending-waits, session_search, recall-hygiene contract
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1380-recall` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2393
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:36:14Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:16:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1380.

## Delivered

**A1 completion — obligations ledger pending-waits (AC5).** A successful `schedule_message` now arms a `pending-wait` obligation whose text is the timer's reason verbatim (from the call arguments) and whose source points at the scheduled-message record — a fired timer re-enters a context that already knows why it exists. `closeObligation` records the closing duty note, so the ledger answers what was *owed*, not just what closed. Structured-engine sessions only (the same engine gate as the rest of the ledger); classic sessions unchanged.

**A2 — `session_search`.** Archive-scale recall over the WHOLE session JSONL chain — hidden, compacted and forked regions included:
- Read-only streamed scan in fixed blocks with byte-level line carry (the `session_chunk_reader` technique — UTF-8 multibyte seams stay intact; verified by a `blockBytes: 7` seam test with non-ASCII content).
- Every line decoded before matching (a raw-line pre-filter would miss matches across JSON escapes); malformed crash-torn tails are skipped, never fatal.
- Result cap + explicit continuation token (re-enters AT the boundary record) + wall-clock budget — an honest `truncated` report instead of a hang.
- `mode: map` reports structure only: record-kind counts, hidden/compacted totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth — the meta layer the agent otherwise improvises with ad-hoc python.
- Hits are pointers (id, kind, timestamp, clipped preview), never content — `compact_expand` stays the only content budget. Scope `branch` filters to the active branch; `tree` spans forks.
- Host without a session file (or a non-`JsonlSessionRepo` backend) degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as `ask`/`request_secret`. Registered under that same always-registered contract in the CLI; the scan itself lives in `session_search.dart` (`searchRecords` pure core + `searchSessionFile` streamed path), exported from the barrel.

**A3 — recall-hygiene prompt contract (AC6).** `prompts/compaction/recall_hygiene.md` → regenerated `recallHygienePrompt` in `prompts.g.dart` (generator spec added; generated const byte-matches the Markdown body): reference = search, the resume ritual over the obligations ledger, commit in the open, the durable-vs-session boundary, the dig idioms. Composed onto the MODE prompt iff the boot-resolved engine is structured — the same expression the compaction driver and the ledger ingest gate on. pi mode is excluded (the benchmark profile strips the compaction tools the contract names — a prompt referencing absent tools lies) and an explicit `systemPrompt` override stays byte-exact (the prompt_overrides suite pins that equality). A classic session's prompt is byte-identical (E3).

## Tests (real coverage for every new behavior; mirror lib/ structure; never real network)

- `test/session/session_search_test.dart` — argument validation (empty/overlong query, invalid regex, bad timestamps), hidden-rule + checkpointed-decision + fork + giant-record coverage, preview clipping, result cap + continuation, branch/tree scope, file-vs-core agreement, non-ranged fallback, malformed tail, UTF-8 seam scans.
- `test/tools/session_search_tool_test.dart` — graceful null host, one-line argument errors, pointer-line formatting, map readout, continuation footer.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_prompt_recall_test.dart` — AC6 gate: structured (default and explicit) composes the contract; classic does not; override stays byte-exact.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_pending_wait_test.dart` + `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_close_obligation_test.dart` + `test/compaction/obligations_ledger_test.dart` — pending-wait arming on `schedule_message`, duty note on close, classic-engine no-op.

`dart analyze` cleanliness and the 80%/90% coverage gate: local dart is unavailable on this box (toolchain broken in this environment) — remote CI verifies.

## Remaining

- Flutter-app host surface (`host_agent_wiring.dart` / app shells): the tool and callback are host-ready (`SessionSearchCallback` seam), but host wiring lands separately — that area is another lane's hot zone this wave.
- Q3 stands as scoped in the issue: v1 keeps the scan index-free (no persisted index to keep consistent); a persistent archive index remains a future slice if scan cost on multi-GB archives proves painful.
- Chunked recall at boot (auto-surface of matching archive pointers) was deliberately not pulled into this slice — the contract teaches the agent to dig; a proactive boot dig is a separate behavioral change.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1458
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1458
- **Title**: feat(1380): total recall for giant sessions — ledger pending-waits, session_search, recall-hygiene contract
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1380-recall` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2393
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:36:14Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:16:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1380.

## Delivered

**A1 completion — obligations ledger pending-waits (AC5).** A successful `schedule_message` now arms a `pending-wait` obligation whose text is the timer's reason verbatim (from the call arguments) and whose source points at the scheduled-message record — a fired timer re-enters a context that already knows why it exists. `closeObligation` records the closing duty note, so the ledger answers what was *owed*, not just what closed. Structured-engine sessions only (the same engine gate as the rest of the ledger); classic sessions unchanged.

**A2 — `session_search`.** Archive-scale recall over the WHOLE session JSONL chain — hidden, compacted and forked regions included:
- Read-only streamed scan in fixed blocks with byte-level line carry (the `session_chunk_reader` technique — UTF-8 multibyte seams stay intact; verified by a `blockBytes: 7` seam test with non-ASCII content).
- Every line decoded before matching (a raw-line pre-filter would miss matches across JSON escapes); malformed crash-torn tails are skipped, never fatal.
- Result cap + explicit continuation token (re-enters AT the boundary record) + wall-clock budget — an honest `truncated` report instead of a hang.
- `mode: map` reports structure only: record-kind counts, hidden/compacted totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth — the meta layer the agent otherwise improvises with ad-hoc python.
- Hits are pointers (id, kind, timestamp, clipped preview), never content — `compact_expand` stays the only content budget. Scope `branch` filters to the active branch; `tree` spans forks.
- Host without a session file (or a non-`JsonlSessionRepo` backend) degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as `ask`/`request_secret`. Registered under that same always-registered contract in the CLI; the scan itself lives in `session_search.dart` (`searchRecords` pure core + `searchSessionFile` streamed path), exported from the barrel.

**A3 — recall-hygiene prompt contract (AC6).** `prompts/compaction/recall_hygiene.md` → regenerated `recallHygienePrompt` in `prompts.g.dart` (generator spec added; generated const byte-matches the Markdown body): reference = search, the resume ritual over the obligations ledger, commit in the open, the durable-vs-session boundary, the dig idioms. Composed onto the MODE prompt iff the boot-resolved engine is structured — the same expression the compaction driver and the ledger ingest gate on. pi mode is excluded (the benchmark profile strips the compaction tools the contract names — a prompt referencing absent tools lies) and an explicit `systemPrompt` override stays byte-exact (the prompt_overrides suite pins that equality). A classic session's prompt is byte-identical (E3).

## Tests (real coverage for every new behavior; mirror lib/ structure; never real network)

- `test/session/session_search_test.dart` — argument validation (empty/overlong query, invalid regex, bad timestamps), hidden-rule + checkpointed-decision + fork + giant-record coverage, preview clipping, result cap + continuation, branch/tree scope, file-vs-core agreement, non-ranged fallback, malformed tail, UTF-8 seam scans.
- `test/tools/session_search_tool_test.dart` — graceful null host, one-line argument errors, pointer-line formatting, map readout, continuation footer.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_prompt_recall_test.dart` — AC6 gate: structured (default and explicit) composes the contract; classic does not; override stays byte-exact.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_pending_wait_test.dart` + `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_close_obligation_test.dart` + `test/compaction/obligations_ledger_test.dart` — pending-wait arming on `schedule_message`, duty note on close, classic-engine no-op.

`dart analyze` cleanliness and the 80%/90% coverage gate: local dart is unavailable on this box (toolchain broken in this environment) — remote CI verifies.

## Remaining

- Flutter-app host surface (`host_agent_wiring.dart` / app shells): the tool and callback are host-ready (`SessionSearchCallback` seam), but host wiring lands separately — that area is another lane's hot zone this wave.
- Q3 stands as scoped in the issue: v1 keeps the scan index-free (no persisted index to keep consistent); a persistent archive index remains a future slice if scan cost on multi-GB archives proves painful.
- Chunked recall at boot (auto-surface of matching archive pointers) was deliberately not pulled into this slice — the contract teaches the agent to dig; a proactive boot dig is a separate behavioral change.

Now I have the main new code. Let me analyze potential issues:

1. **`nextContinuation` semantics**: In `finish()`: `nextContinuation: _stopped && _stopReason == 'result cap' ? recordsTotal - 1 : null`. When result cap stops at a record, `recordsTotal` was already incremented for that record, so `recordsTotal - 1` = number of records examined up to but not including the boundary record. Tool says "resumes the scan after the records already examined" — next call skips `continuation` records. So continuation = recordsTotal - 1 means skip the boundary record next time, re-entering AT the boundary. Wait: next call skips `query.continuation` records (via `_skipped`), then examines from the (continuation+1)-th record. continuation = recordsTotal-1 means skip everything examined, and re-enter at the boundary record. Correct per "re-enters AT the boundary record".

   But note: `recordsExamined` includes... when cap triggers, `recordsTotal++` happened, `_skipped < continuation` false, `recordsExamined++` happened for that record? Let's check seeRecord order: `recordsTotal++`; if skip branch — recordsExamined not incremented. Otherwise recordsExamined++. Then tracking, then cap check before adding hit. When cap hit: `_stop('result cap')`. So recordsExamined includes the boundary record but no hit was added. So continuation = recordsTotal - 1 = recordsExamined - 1 (since no skips) — the boundary record index. OK.

   However, time budget: `nextContinuation` is null on time-budget stop even though partially scanned. Then the footer says "more records may remain (time budget) — narrow with kinds/before/after and search again". That's arguably OK but means no way to continue a time-budget stop. Minor design point, arguably fine.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1458
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1458
- **Title**: feat(1380): total recall for giant sessions — ledger pending-waits, session_search, recall-hygiene contract
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1380-recall` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2393
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:36:14Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:16:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1380.

## Delivered

**A1 completion — obligations ledger pending-waits (AC5).** A successful `schedule_message` now arms a `pending-wait` obligation whose text is the timer's reason verbatim (from the call arguments) and whose source points at the scheduled-message record — a fired timer re-enters a context that already knows why it exists. `closeObligation` records the closing duty note, so the ledger answers what was *owed*, not just what closed. Structured-engine sessions only (the same engine gate as the rest of the ledger); classic sessions unchanged.

**A2 — `session_search`.** Archive-scale recall over the WHOLE session JSONL chain — hidden, compacted and forked regions included:
- Read-only streamed scan in fixed blocks with byte-level line carry (the `session_chunk_reader` technique — UTF-8 multibyte seams stay intact; verified by a `blockBytes: 7` seam test with non-ASCII content).
- Every line decoded before matching (a raw-line pre-filter would miss matches across JSON escapes); malformed crash-torn tails are skipped, never fatal.
- Result cap + explicit continuation token (re-enters AT the boundary record) + wall-clock budget — an honest `truncated` report instead of a hang.
- `mode: map` reports structure only: record-kind counts, hidden/compacted totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth — the meta layer the agent otherwise improvises with ad-hoc python.
- Hits are pointers (id, kind, timestamp, clipped preview), never content — `compact_expand` stays the only content budget. Scope `branch` filters to the active branch; `tree` spans forks.
- Host without a session file (or a non-`JsonlSessionRepo` backend) degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as `ask`/`request_secret`. Registered under that same always-registered contract in the CLI; the scan itself lives in `session_search.dart` (`searchRecords` pure core + `searchSessionFile` streamed path), exported from the barrel.

**A3 — recall-hygiene prompt contract (AC6).** `prompts/compaction/recall_hygiene.md` → regenerated `recallHygienePrompt` in `prompts.g.dart` (generator spec added; generated const byte-matches the Markdown body): reference = search, the resume ritual over the obligations ledger, commit in the open, the durable-vs-session boundary, the dig idioms. Composed onto the MODE prompt iff the boot-resolved engine is structured — the same expression the compaction driver and the ledger ingest gate on. pi mode is excluded (the benchmark profile strips the compaction tools the contract names — a prompt referencing absent tools lies) and an explicit `systemPrompt` override stays byte-exact (the prompt_overrides suite pins that equality). A classic session's prompt is byte-identical (E3).

## Tests (real coverage for every new behavior; mirror lib/ structure; never real network)

- `test/session/session_search_test.dart` — argument validation (empty/overlong query, invalid regex, bad timestamps), hidden-rule + checkpointed-decision + fork + giant-record coverage, preview clipping, result cap + continuation, branch/tree scope, file-vs-core agreement, non-ranged fallback, malformed tail, UTF-8 seam scans.
- `test/tools/session_search_tool_test.dart` — graceful null host, one-line argument errors, pointer-line formatting, map readout, continuation footer.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_prompt_recall_test.dart` — AC6 gate: structured (default and explicit) composes the contract; classic does not; override stays byte-exact.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_pending_wait_test.dart` + `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_close_obligation_test.dart` + `test/compaction/obligations_ledger_test.dart` — pending-wait arming on `schedule_message`, duty note on close, classic-engine no-op.

`dart analyze` cleanliness and the 80%/90% coverage gate: local dart is unavailable on this box (toolchain broken in this environment) — remote CI verifies.

## Remaining

- Flutter-app host surface (`host_agent_wiring.dart` / app shells): the tool and callback are host-ready (`SessionSearchCallback` seam), but host wiring lands separately — that area is another lane's hot zone this wave.
- Q3 stands as scoped in the issue: v1 keeps the scan index-free (no persisted index to keep consistent); a persistent archive index remains a future slice if scan cost on multi-GB archives proves painful.
- Chunked recall at boot (auto-surface of matching archive pointers) was deliberately not pulled into this slice — the contract teaches the agent to dig; a proactive boot dig is a separate behavioral change.

1. **`nextContinuation` semantics**: In `finish()`: `nextContinuation: _stopped && _stopReason == 'result cap' ? recordsTotal - 1 : null`. When result cap stops at a record, `recordsTotal` was already incremented for that record, so `recordsTotal - 1` = number of records examined up to but not including the boundary record. Tool says "resumes the scan after the records already examined" — next call skips `continuation` records. So continuation = recordsTotal - 1 means skip the boundary record next time, re-entering AT the boundary. Wait: next call skips `query.continuation` records (via `_skipped`), then examines from the (continuation+1)-th record. continuation = recordsTotal-1 means skip everything examined, and re-enter at the boundary record. Correct per "re-enters AT the boundary record".

   But note: `recordsExamined` includes... when cap triggers, `recordsTotal++` happened, `_skipped < continuation` false, `recordsExamined++` happened for that record? Let's check seeRecord order: `recordsTotal++`; if skip branch — recordsExamined not incremented. Otherwise recordsExamined++. Then tracking, then cap check before adding hit. When cap hit: `_stop('result cap')`. So recordsExamined includes the boundary record but no hit was added. So continuation = recordsTotal - 1 = recordsExamined - 1 (since no skips) — the boundary record index. OK.

   However, time budget: `nextContinuation` is null on time-budget stop even though partially scanned. Then the footer says "more records may remain (time budget) — narrow with kinds/before/after and search again". That's arguably OK but means no way to continue a time-budget stop. Minor design point, arguably fine.

2. **Bug: time budget deadline checked but hits accumulation uses DateTime.now() only per block; for non-ranged fallback, checked per line. OK.

3. **`_trackTree` — `_activeLeaf` fallback**: `if (_activeLeaf.isEmpty) _activeLeaf = record.id;` — the first record becomes the fallback leaf if no LeafRecord exists. But wait: this line runs for every record until a LeafRecord sets a real leaf. Actually if no LeafRecord ever appears, `_activeLeaf` gets updated every record — ends as the last record. That's a fallback for chains without leaf markers. Hmm, but subtle: if LeafRecord appears early with targetId, then `_activeLeaf` set; fine. But consider: LeafRecord with `targetId` empty? `LeafRecord(:final targetId?)` — pattern with null-check; if targetId is null, doesn't set. OK.

   But there's a real issue: in `seeRecord`, when `_skipped < query.continuation`, tree tracking still runs — good for correctness. However `_trackTree` uses `recordsTotal` for ordinal map: `_ordinalOf[record.id] = recordsTotal - 1`. recordsTotal was already incremented. Fine.

4. **`_branchIds` walk from `_activeLeaf`**: if `_activeLeaf` fallback is the last record and parent chain — fine.

5. **Scope=branch filtering happens AFTER collecting maxHits hits**: In branch scope, hits on forked branches count toward the maxHits cap but are filtered out at finish. So an agent in branch scope may get fewer than maxHits hits and truncation even though more branch hits exist later. This is a correctness/efficiency issue: `seeRecord` checks `_hits.length >= query.maxHits` before filtering by branch. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1458
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1458
- **Title**: feat(1380): total recall for giant sessions — ledger pending-waits, session_search, recall-hygiene contract
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1380-recall` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2393
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:36:14Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:16:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1380.

## Delivered

**A1 completion — obligations ledger pending-waits (AC5).** A successful `schedule_message` now arms a `pending-wait` obligation whose text is the timer's reason verbatim (from the call arguments) and whose source points at the scheduled-message record — a fired timer re-enters a context that already knows why it exists. `closeObligation` records the closing duty note, so the ledger answers what was *owed*, not just what closed. Structured-engine sessions only (the same engine gate as the rest of the ledger); classic sessions unchanged.

**A2 — `session_search`.** Archive-scale recall over the WHOLE session JSONL chain — hidden, compacted and forked regions included:
- Read-only streamed scan in fixed blocks with byte-level line carry (the `session_chunk_reader` technique — UTF-8 multibyte seams stay intact; verified by a `blockBytes: 7` seam test with non-ASCII content).
- Every line decoded before matching (a raw-line pre-filter would miss matches across JSON escapes); malformed crash-torn tails are skipped, never fatal.
- Result cap + explicit continuation token (re-enters AT the boundary record) + wall-clock budget — an honest `truncated` report instead of a hang.
- `mode: map` reports structure only: record-kind counts, hidden/compacted totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth — the meta layer the agent otherwise improvises with ad-hoc python.
- Hits are pointers (id, kind, timestamp, clipped preview), never content — `compact_expand` stays the only content budget. Scope `branch` filters to the active branch; `tree` spans forks.
- Host without a session file (or a non-`JsonlSessionRepo` backend) degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as `ask`/`request_secret`. Registered under that same always-registered contract in the CLI; the scan itself lives in `session_search.dart` (`searchRecords` pure core + `searchSessionFile` streamed path), exported from the barrel.

**A3 — recall-hygiene prompt contract (AC6).** `prompts/compaction/recall_hygiene.md` → regenerated `recallHygienePrompt` in `prompts.g.dart` (generator spec added; generated const byte-matches the Markdown body): reference = search, the resume ritual over the obligations ledger, commit in the open, the durable-vs-session boundary, the dig idioms. Composed onto the MODE prompt iff the boot-resolved engine is structured — the same expression the compaction driver and the ledger ingest gate on. pi mode is excluded (the benchmark profile strips the compaction tools the contract names — a prompt referencing absent tools lies) and an explicit `systemPrompt` override stays byte-exact (the prompt_overrides suite pins that equality). A classic session's prompt is byte-identical (E3).

## Tests (real coverage for every new behavior; mirror lib/ structure; never real network)

- `test/session/session_search_test.dart` — argument validation (empty/overlong query, invalid regex, bad timestamps), hidden-rule + checkpointed-decision + fork + giant-record coverage, preview clipping, result cap + continuation, branch/tree scope, file-vs-core agreement, non-ranged fallback, malformed tail, UTF-8 seam scans.
- `test/tools/session_search_tool_test.dart` — graceful null host, one-line argument errors, pointer-line formatting, map readout, continuation footer.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_prompt_recall_test.dart` — AC6 gate: structured (default and explicit) composes the contract; classic does not; override stays byte-exact.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_pending_wait_test.dart` + `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_close_obligation_test.dart` + `test/compaction/obligations_ledger_test.dart` — pending-wait arming on `schedule_message`, duty note on close, classic-engine no-op.

`dart analyze` cleanliness and the 80%/90% coverage gate: local dart is unavailable on this box (toolchain broken in this environment) — remote CI verifies.

## Remaining

- Flutter-app host surface (`host_agent_wiring.dart` / app shells): the tool and callback are host-ready (`SessionSearchCallback` seam), but host wiring lands separately — that area is another lane's hot zone this wave.
- Q3 stands as scoped in the issue: v1 keeps the scan index-free (no persisted index to keep consistent); a persistent archive index remains a future slice if scan cost on multi-GB archives proves painful.
- Chunked recall at boot (auto-surface of matching archive pointers) was deliberately not pulled into this slice — the contract teaches the agent to dig; a proactive boot dig is a separate behavioral change.

1. **`nextContinuation` semantics**: In `finish()`: `nextContinuation: _stopped && _stopReason == 'result cap' ? recordsTotal - 1 : null`. When result cap stops at a record, `recordsTotal` was already incremented for that record, so `recordsTotal - 1` = number of records examined up to but not including the boundary record. Tool says "resumes the scan after the records already examined" — next call skips `continuation` records. So continuation = recordsTotal - 1 means skip the boundary record next time, re-entering AT the boundary. Wait: next call skips `query.continuation` records (via `_skipped`), then examines from the (continuation+1)-th record. continuation = recordsTotal-1 means skip everything examined, and re-enter at the boundary record. Correct per "re-enters AT the boundary record".

   But note: `recordsExamined` includes... when cap triggers, `recordsTotal++` happened, `_skipped < continuation` false, `recordsExamined++` happened for that record? Let's check seeRecord order: `recordsTotal++`; if skip branch — recordsExamined not incremented. Otherwise recordsExamined++. Then tracking, then cap check before adding hit. When cap hit: `_stop('result cap')`. So recordsExamined includes the boundary record but no hit was added. So continuation = recordsTotal - 1 = recordsExamined - 1 (since no skips) — the boundary record index. OK.

   However, time budget: `nextContinuation` is null on time-budget stop even though partially scanned. Then the footer says "more records may remain (time budget) — narrow with kinds/before/after and search again". That's arguably OK but means no way to continue a time-budget stop. Minor design point, arguably fine.

2. **Bug: time budget deadline checked but hits accumulation uses DateTime.now() only per block; for non-ranged fallback, checked per line. OK.

3. **`_trackTree` — `_activeLeaf` fallback**: `if (_activeLeaf.isEmpty) _activeLeaf = record.id;` — the first record becomes the fallback leaf if no LeafRecord exists. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1458
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1458
- **Title**: feat(1380): total recall for giant sessions — ledger pending-waits, session_search, recall-hygiene contract
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1380-recall` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2393
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:36:14Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:16:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1380.

## Delivered

**A1 completion — obligations ledger pending-waits (AC5).** A successful `schedule_message` now arms a `pending-wait` obligation whose text is the timer's reason verbatim (from the call arguments) and whose source points at the scheduled-message record — a fired timer re-enters a context that already knows why it exists. `closeObligation` records the closing duty note, so the ledger answers what was *owed*, not just what closed. Structured-engine sessions only (the same engine gate as the rest of the ledger); classic sessions unchanged.

**A2 — `session_search`.** Archive-scale recall over the WHOLE session JSONL chain — hidden, compacted and forked regions included:
- Read-only streamed scan in fixed blocks with byte-level line carry (the `session_chunk_reader` technique — UTF-8 multibyte seams stay intact; verified by a `blockBytes: 7` seam test with non-ASCII content).
- Every line decoded before matching (a raw-line pre-filter would miss matches across JSON escapes); malformed crash-torn tails are skipped, never fatal.
- Result cap + explicit continuation token (re-enters AT the boundary record) + wall-clock budget — an honest `truncated` report instead of a hang.
- `mode: map` reports structure only: record-kind counts, hidden/compacted totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth — the meta layer the agent otherwise improvises with ad-hoc python.
- Hits are pointers (id, kind, timestamp, clipped preview), never content — `compact_expand` stays the only content budget. Scope `branch` filters to the active branch; `tree` spans forks.
- Host without a session file (or a non-`JsonlSessionRepo` backend) degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as `ask`/`request_secret`. Registered under that same always-registered contract in the CLI; the scan itself lives in `session_search.dart` (`searchRecords` pure core + `searchSessionFile` streamed path), exported from the barrel.

**A3 — recall-hygiene prompt contract (AC6).** `prompts/compaction/recall_hygiene.md` → regenerated `recallHygienePrompt` in `prompts.g.dart` (generator spec added; generated const byte-matches the Markdown body): reference = search, the resume ritual over the obligations ledger, commit in the open, the durable-vs-session boundary, the dig idioms. Composed onto the MODE prompt iff the boot-resolved engine is structured — the same expression the compaction driver and the ledger ingest gate on. pi mode is excluded (the benchmark profile strips the compaction tools the contract names — a prompt referencing absent tools lies) and an explicit `systemPrompt` override stays byte-exact (the prompt_overrides suite pins that equality). A classic session's prompt is byte-identical (E3).

## Tests (real coverage for every new behavior; mirror lib/ structure; never real network)

- `test/session/session_search_test.dart` — argument validation (empty/overlong query, invalid regex, bad timestamps), hidden-rule + checkpointed-decision + fork + giant-record coverage, preview clipping, result cap + continuation, branch/tree scope, file-vs-core agreement, non-ranged fallback, malformed tail, UTF-8 seam scans.
- `test/tools/session_search_tool_test.dart` — graceful null host, one-line argument errors, pointer-line formatting, map readout, continuation footer.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_prompt_recall_test.dart` — AC6 gate: structured (default and explicit) composes the contract; classic does not; override stays byte-exact.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_pending_wait_test.dart` + `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_close_obligation_test.dart` + `test/compaction/obligations_ledger_test.dart` — pending-wait arming on `schedule_message`, duty note on close, classic-engine no-op.

`dart analyze` cleanliness and the 80%/90% coverage gate: local dart is unavailable on this box (toolchain broken in this environment) — remote CI verifies.

## Remaining

- Flutter-app host surface (`host_agent_wiring.dart` / app shells): the tool and callback are host-ready (`SessionSearchCallback` seam), but host wiring lands separately — that area is another lane's hot zone this wave.
- Q3 stands as scoped in the issue: v1 keeps the scan index-free (no persisted index to keep consistent); a persistent archive index remains a future slice if scan cost on multi-GB archives proves painful.
- Chunked recall at boot (auto-surface of matching archive pointers) was deliberately not pulled into this slice — the contract teaches the agent to dig; a proactive boot dig is a separate behavioral change.

## PR Description

Fixes #1380.

## Delivered

**A1 completion — obligations ledger pending-waits (AC5).** A successful `schedule_message` now arms a `pending-wait` obligation whose text is the timer's reason verbatim (from the call arguments) and whose source points at the scheduled-message record — a fired timer re-enters a context that already knows why it exists. `closeObligation` records the closing duty note, so the ledger answers what was *owed*, not just what closed. Structured-engine sessions only (the same engine gate as the rest of the ledger); classic sessions unchanged.

**A2 — `session_search`.** Archive-scale recall over the WHOLE session JSONL chain — hidden, compacted and forked regions included:
- Read-only streamed scan in fixed blocks with byte-level line carry (the `session_chunk_reader` technique — UTF-8 multibyte seams stay intact; verified by a `blockBytes: 7` seam test with non-ASCII content).
- Every line decoded before matching (a raw-line pre-filter would miss matches across JSON escapes); malformed crash-torn tails are skipped, never fatal.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1458
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1458
- **Title**: feat(1380): total recall for giant sessions — ledger pending-waits, session_search, recall-hygiene contract
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1380-recall` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2393
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:36:14Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:16:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1380.

## Delivered

**A1 completion — obligations ledger pending-waits (AC5).** A successful `schedule_message` now arms a `pending-wait` obligation whose text is the timer's reason verbatim (from the call arguments) and whose source points at the scheduled-message record — a fired timer re-enters a context that already knows why it exists. `closeObligation` records the closing duty note, so the ledger answers what was *owed*, not just what closed. Structured-engine sessions only (the same engine gate as the rest of the ledger); classic sessions unchanged.

**A2 — `session_search`.** Archive-scale recall over the WHOLE session JSONL chain — hidden, compacted and forked regions included:
- Read-only streamed scan in fixed blocks with byte-level line carry (the `session_chunk_reader` technique — UTF-8 multibyte seams stay intact; verified by a `blockBytes: 7` seam test with non-ASCII content).
- Every line decoded before matching (a raw-line pre-filter would miss matches across JSON escapes); malformed crash-torn tails are skipped, never fatal.
- Result cap + explicit continuation token (re-enters AT the boundary record) + wall-clock budget — an honest `truncated` report instead of a hang.
- `mode: map` reports structure only: record-kind counts, hidden/compacted totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth — the meta layer the agent otherwise improvises with ad-hoc python.
- Hits are pointers (id, kind, timestamp, clipped preview), never content — `compact_expand` stays the only content budget. Scope `branch` filters to the active branch; `tree` spans forks.
- Host without a session file (or a non-`JsonlSessionRepo` backend) degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as `ask`/`request_secret`. Registered under that same always-registered contract in the CLI; the scan itself lives in `session_search.dart` (`searchRecords` pure core + `searchSessionFile` streamed path), exported from the barrel.

**A3 — recall-hygiene prompt contract (AC6).** `prompts/compaction/recall_hygiene.md` → regenerated `recallHygienePrompt` in `prompts.g.dart` (generator spec added; generated const byte-matches the Markdown body): reference = search, the resume ritual over the obligations ledger, commit in the open, the durable-vs-session boundary, the dig idioms. Composed onto the MODE prompt iff the boot-resolved engine is structured — the same expression the compaction driver and the ledger ingest gate on. pi mode is excluded (the benchmark profile strips the compaction tools the contract names — a prompt referencing absent tools lies) and an explicit `systemPrompt` override stays byte-exact (the prompt_overrides suite pins that equality). A classic session's prompt is byte-identical (E3).

## Tests (real coverage for every new behavior; mirror lib/ structure; never real network)

- `test/session/session_search_test.dart` — argument validation (empty/overlong query, invalid regex, bad timestamps), hidden-rule + checkpointed-decision + fork + giant-record coverage, preview clipping, result cap + continuation, branch/tree scope, file-vs-core agreement, non-ranged fallback, malformed tail, UTF-8 seam scans.
- `test/tools/session_search_tool_test.dart` — graceful null host, one-line argument errors, pointer-line formatting, map readout, continuation footer.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_prompt_recall_test.dart` — AC6 gate: structured (default and explicit) composes the contract; classic does not; override stays byte-exact.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_pending_wait_test.dart` + `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_close_obligation_test.dart` + `test/compaction/obligations_ledger_test.dart` — pending-wait arming on `schedule_message`, duty note on close, classic-engine no-op.

`dart analyze` cleanliness and the 80%/90% coverage gate: local dart is unavailable on this box (toolchain broken in this environment) — remote CI verifies.

## Remaining

- Flutter-app host surface (`host_agent_wiring.dart` / app shells): the tool and callback are host-ready (`SessionSearchCallback` seam), but host wiring lands separately — that area is another lane's hot zone this wave.
- Q3 stands as scoped in the issue: v1 keeps the scan index-free (no persisted index to keep consistent); a persistent archive index remains a future slice if scan cost on multi-GB archives proves painful.
- Chunked recall at boot (auto-surface of matching archive pointers) was deliberately not pulled into this slice — the contract teaches the agent to dig; a proactive boot dig is a separate behavioral change.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1458
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1458
- **Title**: feat(1380): total recall for giant sessions — ledger pending-waits, session_search, recall-hygiene contract
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1380-recall` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2393
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:36:14Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:16:35Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1380.

## Delivered

**A1 completion — obligations ledger pending-waits (AC5).** A successful `schedule_message` now arms a `pending-wait` obligation whose text is the timer's reason verbatim (from the call arguments) and whose source points at the scheduled-message record — a fired timer re-enters a context that already knows why it exists. `closeObligation` records the closing duty note, so the ledger answers what was *owed*, not just what closed. Structured-engine sessions only (the same engine gate as the rest of the ledger); classic sessions unchanged.

**A2 — `session_search`.** Archive-scale recall over the WHOLE session JSONL chain — hidden, compacted and forked regions included:
- Read-only streamed scan in fixed blocks with byte-level line carry (the `session_chunk_reader` technique — UTF-8 multibyte seams stay intact; verified by a `blockBytes: 7` seam test with non-ASCII content).
- Every line decoded before matching (a raw-line pre-filter would miss matches across JSON escapes); malformed crash-torn tails are skipped, never fatal.
- Result cap + explicit continuation token (re-enters AT the boundary record) + wall-clock budget — an honest `truncated` report instead of a hang.
- `mode: map` reports structure only: record-kind counts, hidden/compacted totals, checkpoint tree with nesting depth — the meta layer the agent otherwise improvises with ad-hoc python.
- Hits are pointers (id, kind, timestamp, clipped preview), never content — `compact_expand` stays the only content budget. Scope `branch` filters to the active branch; `tree` spans forks.
- Host without a session file (or a non-`JsonlSessionRepo` backend) degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as `ask`/`request_secret`. Registered under that same always-registered contract in the CLI; the scan itself lives in `session_search.dart` (`searchRecords` pure core + `searchSessionFile` streamed path), exported from the barrel.

**A3 — recall-hygiene prompt contract (AC6).** `prompts/compaction/recall_hygiene.md` → regenerated `recallHygienePrompt` in `prompts.g.dart` (generator spec added; generated const byte-matches the Markdown body): reference = search, the resume ritual over the obligations ledger, commit in the open, the durable-vs-session boundary, the dig idioms. Composed onto the MODE prompt iff the boot-resolved engine is structured — the same expression the compaction driver and the ledger ingest gate on. pi mode is excluded (the benchmark profile strips the compaction tools the contract names — a prompt referencing absent tools lies) and an explicit `systemPrompt` override stays byte-exact (the prompt_overrides suite pins that equality). A classic session's prompt is byte-identical (E3).

## Tests (real coverage for every new behavior; mirror lib/ structure; never real network)

- `test/session/session_search_test.dart` — argument validation (empty/overlong query, invalid regex, bad timestamps), hidden-rule + checkpointed-decision + fork + giant-record coverage, preview clipping, result cap + continuation, branch/tree scope, file-vs-core agreement, non-ranged fallback, malformed tail, UTF-8 seam scans.
- `test/tools/session_search_tool_test.dart` — graceful null host, one-line argument errors, pointer-line formatting, map readout, continuation footer.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_prompt_recall_test.dart` — AC6 gate: structured (default and explicit) composes the contract; classic does not; override stays byte-exact.
- `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_pending_wait_test.dart` + `test/cli/agent_cli_persist_close_obligation_test.dart` + `test/compaction/obligations_ledger_test.dart` — pending-wait arming on `schedule_message`, duty note on close, classic-engine no-op.

`dart analyze` cleanliness and the 80%/90% coverage gate: local dart is unavailable on this box (toolchain broken in this environment) — remote CI verifies.

## Remaining

- Flutter-app host surface (`host_agent_wiring.dart` / app shells): the tool and callback are host-ready (`SessionSearchCallback` seam), but host wiring lands separately — that area is another lane's hot zone this wave.
- Q3 stands as scoped in the issue: v1 keeps the scan index-free (no persisted index to keep consistent); a persistent archive index remains a future slice if scan cost on multi-GB archives proves painful.
- Chunked recall at boot (auto-surface of matching archive pointers) was deliberately not pulled into this slice — the contract teaches the agent to dig; a proactive boot dig is a separate behavioral change.

Now I have the main new code. Let me analyze potential issues:

1. **`nextContinuation` semantics**: In `finish()`: `nextContinuation: _stopped && _stopReason == 'result cap' ? recordsTotal - 1 : null`. When result cap stops at a record, `recordsTotal` was already incremented for that record, so `recordsTotal - 1` = number of records examined up to but not including the boundary record. Tool says "resumes the scan after the records already examined" — next call skips `continuation` records. So continuation = recordsTotal - 1 means skip the boundary record next time, re-entering AT the boundary. Wait: next call skips `query.continuation` records (via `_skipped`), then examines from the (continuation+1)-th record. continuation = recordsTotal-1 means skip everything examined, and re-enter at the boundary record. Correct per "re-enters AT the boundary record".

   But note: `recordsExamined` includes... when cap triggers, `recordsTotal++` happened, `_skipped < continuation` false, `recordsExamined++` happened for that record? Let's check seeRecord order: `recordsTotal++`; if skip branch — recordsExamined not incremented. Otherwise recordsExamined++. Then tracking, then cap check before adding hit. When cap hit: `_stop('result cap')`. So recordsExamined includes the boundary record but no hit was added. So continuation = recordsTotal - 1 = recordsExamined - 1 (since no skips) — the boundary record index. OK.

   However, time budget: `nextContinuation` is null on time-budget stop even though partially scanned. Then the footer says "more records may remain (time budget) — narrow with kinds/before/after and search again". That's arguably OK but means no way to continue a time-budget stop. Minor design point, arguably fine.

2. **Bug: time budget deadline checked but hits accumulation uses DateTime.now() only per block; for non-ranged fallback, checked per line. OK.

3. **`_trackTree` — `_activeLeaf` fallback**: `if (_activeLeaf.isEmpty) _activeLeaf = record.id;` — the first record becomes the fallback leaf if no LeafRecord exists. But wait: this line runs for every record until a LeafRecord sets a real leaf. Actually if no LeafRecord ever appears, `_activeLeaf` gets updated every record — ends as the last record. That's a fallback for chains without leaf markers. Hmm, but subtle: if LeafRecord appears early with targetId, then `_activeLeaf` set; fine. But consider: LeafRecord with `targetId` empty? `LeafRecord(:final targetId?)` — pattern with null-check; if targetId is null, doesn't set. OK.

   But there's a real issue: in `seeRecord`, when `_skipped < query.continuation`, tree tracking still runs — good for correctness. However `_trackTree` uses `recordsTotal` for ordinal map: `_ordinalOf[record.id] = recordsTotal - 1`. recordsTotal was already incremented. Fine.

Now, a key correctness check for `_trackTree` and the fallback `_activeLeaf`: `if (_activeLeaf.isEmpty) _activeLeaf = record.id;` — the first record seen becomes the provisional leaf, updated on each record until a LeafRecord sets a definitive one. But the ORDER matters: a LeafRecord with `targetId: null` (tree root) — pattern `LeafRecord(:final targetId?)` requires targetId non-null, so root-leaf doesn't clear the provisional leaf. If the session navigated to root, `_activeLeaf` stays at whatever it was — arguably the whole tree; edge case, fine.

But there's a subtle bug: `_trackTree` is called for skipped records too (continuation), and `_activeLeaf` fallback `if (_activeLeaf.isEmpty)` — first record sets it; subsequent records don't override unless a LeafRecord appears. In a forked chain without leaf records, leaf = last record. OK.

Bigger question — the branch-scope + maxHits interplay (finding 5). Let me confirm: `seeRecord` adds hits to `_hits` regardless of scope; the cap counts `_hits.length` — including hits that will be filtered out at finish for branch scope. So yes, under `scope: branch` (the DEFAULT), fork-branch hits consume the hit budget, causing premature 'result cap' with fewer than maxHits returned hits and a continuation token that forces a full re-scan. This is a genuine IMPORTANT finding: the default scope under-delivers and burns the 10s budget re-scanning.

Wait — actually is it premature "result cap"? `_stop('result cap')` when `_hits.length >= query.maxHits` and the current record matches. So scanning stops at maxHits total matches (branch + fork), finish filters to branch hits → could return far fewer. And `truncated: true` with continuation. Agent continues; next scan skips `continuation` records (ALL records, not just branch), so it works, but each page costs a full re-scan of the prefix — O(n²) total for paging through. Given time budget 10s per call, this is a real efficiency flaw in the feature's headline scenario (forked giant sessions). IMPORTANT.

Also the `recordsExamined` count reported includes non-branch records; fine.

Next: `nextContinuation` for 'result cap' = `recordsTotal - 1`. But when stopped by result cap, also `_skipped` handling with continuation: in a continued scan, `_skipped` counts records skipped; `recordsTotal` counts all records seen including skipped ones. Continuation semantics consistent.

But note an off-by-one consideration: on the continued call, `_skipped < query.continuation` skip; the boundary record (index recordsTotal-1, 0-based) is the first examined. Correct.

Another subtle issue: on a continued scan that ALSO hits the cap, `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` where recordsTotal includes skipped — fine.

But what about time-budget truncation on a continued scan — no continuation given; the footer tells the agent to narrow with kinds/before/after. With before/after filters the agent can progress. Acceptable, though inconsistent that 'result cap' pages and 'time budget' doesn't. SUGGESTION.

Now the "no session file" outcome formatting issue (finding: searchSessionArchive returns truncated:false, reason 'no session file' → formatter prints "no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)"). The truncationReason is never shown. The model is told the archive is empty rather than unbacked. Contradicts the PR's "honest cannot-search result" claim. IMPORTANT.

Wait — check: does the CLI pass search: searchSessionArchive always? Yes: `sessionSearchTool(search: searchSessionArchive)`. So a memory-backed host (no JsonlSessionRepo) prints "no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)". Hmm, that's actively misleading. The tool-level null callback case is handled gracefully ('This host has no session file to search.'), but the real CLI path never has a null callback — it has searchSessionArchive which returns the dishonest outcome. So the graceful degradation in practice yields "no records match". Definitely IMPORTANT.

Fix suggestion: in formatSessionSearchOutcome, when recordsTotal == 0 && truncationReason.isNotEmpty → print the reason; or set truncated: true? Or the tool checks `outcome.truncationReason == 'no session file'`. Simplest: in `searchSessionArchive` keep contract by formatting... but formatting is in the tool. Alternative: make formatSessionSearchOutcome print truncationReason when hits empty and reason non-empty. Or the CLI could return null outcome → but signature non-null. Fine, that's the fix area.

Next: `recordPendingWait` — return values discarded. The doc comments say "Returns the human-readable outcome for the attach site; failures are REPORTED here and swallowed by the afterToolCall wrapper". But `_attachObligationPendingWaits` ignores the return entirely — so "REPORTED" is false; nothing is ever reported. Dead code / misleading docs. SUGGESTION (or IMPORTANT-lite). It's maintainability: either log via the CLI's logger or drop the return values. Check if AgentCli has a logger — likely `_log` or similar. I'd mark SUGGESTION.

Also `recordPendingWait` regex coupling: `^scheduled (\S+) for ` depends on schedule_message_tool's human-readable line. If the tool's wording changes (e.g. localization, sender suffix ordering), pending-wait silently stops arming with only a discarded string as signal. Tests pin current behavior, so it won't regress silently in CI — SUGGESTION.

Security review:
- No shell interpolation, no secrets, read-only scan. The preview could contain sensitive content but redaction pipeline handles tool output (as PR states). 
- The `read $FAH_SESSION_FILE:<line>` prompt hint — fine.
- DoS: regex bounded by 128KB text cap + 10s wall budget. But note: `pattern.hasMatch` on a 128KB string with catastrophic backtracking — Dart's RegExp is... Dart uses JavaScript-compatible regex (irregexp-like?) Actually Dart's RegExp is implemented via... it can exhibit exponential backtracking. The 10s deadline is only checked BETWEEN lines/blocks, not during a single hasMatch — a single catastrophic regex on a 128KB text could hang far beyond 10 seconds? Dart's RegExp is the irregexp port? No — Dart native VM uses... Dart's RegExp on the standalone VM is implemented with a backtracking engine? Actually Dart uses "irregexp"-style? Let me think. Dart's RegExp in the VM: `dart:core` RegExp is implemented over the VM's internal regexp which IS a backtracking engine for some features; it has optimizations but catastrophic backtracking is possible. A single 128KB subject with nested quantifiers could take effectively forever (minutes/hours), and the deadline check after seeLine won't run until the match completes. So the "E5: never a hang" claim is not fully honored for a single record. Mitigation: cap per-record text for regex to something much smaller, or check deadline... can't interrupt mid-match. Realistically: 128KB cap with exponential backtracking — e.g. `(a+)+$` on 128KB of 'a' — that's ~2^128K ops — hang. This is a genuine BLOCKING-level DoS? The threat model: the agent itself issues the query (regex: true) — self-inflicted. The query comes from the model, not an attacker. A model could accidentally produce catastrophic regex and hang its own CLI for effectively forever (not just 10s). Impact: the process hangs mid-tool-call until killed. Given the PR explicitly claims "a time budget stops pathological regexes (E5) with an honest truncated report instead of a hang" — the claim is wrong for single-record matches. Severity: IMPORTANT (the budget doesn't do what it claims; but attacker model is the agent itself). I'd say IMPORTANT, possibly BLOCKING given the PR's explicit E5 claim and "never a hang" promise. Hmm. The scan streams blocks; the deadline check happens after each line and each block. Within one line, hasMatch can hang unboundedly. Since the agent authors its own regex, accidental catastrophic backtracking is plausible (models write `(a|b)*c`-style patterns). I'll classify as IMPORTANT (correctness/robustness), leaning BLOCKING? The verdict rules: BLOCKING = broken behavior. A hang is broken behavior but requires a pathological self-authored regex on a giant record. The PR explicitly sells "never a hang" — I'd rate it BLOCKING for the false E5 guarant…

Now, a key correctness check for `_trackTree` and the fallback `_activeLeaf`: `if (_activeLeaf.isEmpty) _activeLeaf = record.id;` — the first record seen becomes the provisional leaf, updated on each record until a LeafRecord sets a definitive one. If the session navigated to root, `_activeLeaf` stays at whatever it was — arguably the whole tree; edge case, fine.

But there's a subtle bug: `_trackTree` is called for skipped records too (continuation), and `_activeLeaf` fallback `if (_activeLeaf.isEmpty)` — first record sets it; subsequent records don't override unless a LeafRecord appears. In a forked chain without leaf records, leaf = last record. OK.

Bigger question — the branch-scope + maxHits interplay (finding 5). Let me confirm: `seeRecord` adds hits to `_hits` regardless of scope; the cap counts `_hits.length` — including hits that will be filtered out at finish for branch scope. So yes, under `scope: branch` (the DEFAULT), fork-branch hits consume the hit budget, causing premature 'result cap' with fewer than maxHits returned hits and a continuation token that forces a full re-scan. This is a genuine IMPORTANT finding: the default scope under-delivers and burns the 10s budget re-scanning.

Wait — actually is it premature "result cap"? `_stop('result cap')` when `_hits.length >= query.maxHits` and the current record matches. So scanning stops at maxHits total matches (branch + fork), finish filters to branch hits → could return far fewer. And `truncated: true` with continuation. Agent continues; next scan skips `continuation` records (ALL records, not just branch), so it works, but each page costs a full re-scan of the prefix — O(n²) total for paging through. Given time budget 10s per call, this is a real efficiency flaw in the feature's headline scenario (forked giant sessions). IMPORTANT.

Also the `recordsExamined` count reported includes non-branch records; fine.

Next: `nextContinuation` for 'result cap' = `recordsTotal - 1`. But when stopped by result cap, also `_skipped` handling with continuation: in a continued scan, `_skipped` counts records skipped; `recordsTotal` counts all records seen including skipped ones. Continuation semantics consistent.

But note an off-by-one consideration: on the continued call, `_skipped < query.continuation` skip; the boundary record (index recordsTotal-1, 0-based) is the first examined. Correct.

Another subtle issue: on a continued scan that ALSO hits the cap, `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` where recordsTotal includes skipped — fine.

But what about time-budget truncation on a continued scan — no continuation given; the footer tells the agent to narrow with kinds/before/after. With before/after filters the agent can progress. Acceptable, though inconsistent that 'result cap' pages and 'time budget' doesn't. SUGGESTION.

Now, a key correctness check for `_trackTree` and the fallback `_activeLeaf`: `if (_activeLeaf.isEmpty) _activeLeaf = record.id;` — the first record seen becomes the provisional leaf, updated on each record until a LeafRecord sets a definitive one. But the ORDER matters: a LeafRecord with `targetId: null` (tree root) — pattern `LeafRecord(:final targetId?)` requires targetId non-null, so root-leaf doesn't clear the provisional leaf. If the session navigated to root, `_activeLeaf` stays at whatever it was — arguably the whole tree; edge case, fine.

But there's a subtle bug: `_trackTree` is called for skipped records too (continuation), and `_activeLeaf` fallback `if (_activeLeaf.isEmpty)` — first record sets it; subsequent records don't override unless a LeafRecord appears. In a forked chain without leaf records, leaf = last record. OK.

Bigger question — the branch-scope + maxHits interplay (finding 5). Let me confirm: `seeRecord` adds hits to `_hits` regardless of scope; the cap counts `_hits.length` — including hits that will be filtered out at finish for branch scope. So yes, under `scope: branch` (the DEFAULT), fork-branch hits consume the hit budget, causing premature 'result cap' with fewer than maxHits returned hits and a continuation token that forces a full re-scan. This is a genuine IMPORTANT finding: the default scope under-delivers and burns the 10s budget re-scanning.

Wait — actually is it premature "result cap"? `_stop('result cap')` when `_hits.length >= query.maxHits` and the current record matches. So scanning stops at maxHits total matches (branch + fork), finish filters to branch hits → could return far fewer. And `truncated: true` with continuation. Agent continues; next scan skips `continuation` records (ALL records, not just branch), so it works, but each page costs a full re-scan of the prefix — O(n²) total for paging through. Given time budget 10s per call, this is a real efficiency flaw in the feature's headline scenario (forked giant sessions). IMPORTANT.

Also the `recordsExamined` count reported includes non-branch records; fine.

Next: `nextContinuation` for 'result cap' = `recordsTotal - 1`. But when stopped by result cap, also `_skipped` handling with continuation: in a continued scan, `_skipped` counts records skipped; `recordsTotal` counts all records seen including skipped ones. Continuation semantics consistent.

But note an off-by-one consideration: on the continued call, `_skipped < query.continuation` skip; the boundary record (index recordsTotal-1, 0-based) is the first examined. Correct.

Another subtle issue: on a continued scan that ALSO hits the cap, `nextContinuation = recordsTotal - 1` where recordsTotal includes skipped — fine.

Agent continues; next scan skips `continuation` records (ALL records, not just branch), so it works, but each page costs a full re-scan of the prefix — O(n²) total for paging through. Given time budget 10s per call, this is a real efficiency flaw in the feature's headline scenario (forked giant sessions). IMPORTANT.

C. **Branch-scope hit cap counts fork hits** (default scope!) — IMPORTANT. `seeRecord` caps on `_hits.length` before the branch filter in `finish()`, so under the default `scope: branch`, fork-only matches consume the 40-hit budget → premature 'result cap', fewer branch hits returned, and each continuation page re-scans from the chain start (continuation skip is global), O(n²) paging under a 10s budget. Fix: apply branch membership at collection time (needs leaf known — leaf may appear after hits... leaf records typically appear... hmm, the leaf marker could appear anywhere; deferred filtering is why they did it post-hoc). Alternative: on cap, only stop when `_hits.length >= maxHits` AND... they can't know branch membership yet. Could over-collect (maxHits branch + some slack) or walk from provisional leaf. At minimum document; better: collect up to maxHits but on finish, if scope=branch and filtered count < collected, continue scanning? Complex. I'll flag as IMPORTANT with suggestion.

D. **Regex DoS: per-record 128KB cap + backtracking engine defeats the 10s wall-clock budget** — the deadline is only checked between lines/blocks; a single `pattern.hasMatch` on a 128KB record with catastrophic backtracking hangs unboundedly, contradicting the E5 "never a hang" claim. C. **Branch-scope hit cap counts fork hits** (default scope!) — IMPORTANT. `seeRecord` caps on `_hits.length` before the branch filter in `finish()`, so under the default `scope: branch`, fork-only matches consume the 40-hit budget → premature 'result cap', fewer branch hits returned, and each continuation page re-scans from the chain start (continuation skip is global), O(n²) paging under a 10s budget. Fix: apply branch membership at collection time (needs leaf known — leaf may appear after hits... leaf records typically appear... hmm, the leaf marker could appear anywhere; deferred filtering is why they did it post-hoc). Alternative: on cap, only stop when `_hits.length >= maxHits` AND... they can't know branch membership yet. Could over-collect (maxHits branch + some slack) or walk from provisional leaf. At minimum document; better: collect up to maxHits but on finish, if scope=branch and filtered count < collected, continue scanning? Complex. I'll flag as IMPORTANT with suggestion.

D. **Regex DoS: per-record 128KB cap + backtracking engine defeats the 10s wall-clock budget** — the deadline is only checked between lines/blocks; a single `pattern.hasMatch` on a 128KB record with catastrophic backtracking hangs unboundedly, contradicting the E5 "never a hang" claim. A self-inflicted DoS that wedges the whole agent runtime, in a feature whose stated goal is robustness against pathological inputs (E5), is a correctness gap. ## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The design and test intent are strong, but the PR's own test suite is red: three new test files fail to compile/load (duplicate `payload` local in `obligations_ledger_test.dart`, non-const `const _giantText = 'x' * 2000` in `session_search_test.dart`, missing `prompts.g.dart` import in `agent_cli_prompt_recall_test.dart`) and the capped-scan formatting test fails at runtime because the empty-hits early return drops the truncation/continuation footer. All four verified locally with `dart analyze` / `dart test` (the toolchain works fine on this box).

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 4 blocking: 3 test-compile/load failures + the truncated-footer formatting bug (inline comments 01–04)
- ⚠️ 4 important: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match"; the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter (default scope under-delivers); the 128 KB regex cap + 10 s budget cannot interrupt one catastrophic-backtracking match, so the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not honored; the accumulator's `_parentOf`/`_ordinalOf` maps grow linearly with archive size, contradicting the flat-memory claim for giant sessions
- 💡 5 suggestions: discarded pending-wait report strings, O(n²) checkpoint list building, no continuation token on time-budget stops, `scanSessionSegment` exposing a private type in the public barrel API, and the regex-parse coupling to `schedule_message`'s result wording

**Next Steps**:
1. Fix the three test files so they compile/load (one-line fixes each) and fix the empty-hits truncation footer in `formatSessionSearchOutcome`
2. Surface `truncationReason` when the archive is unavailable, cap branch hits at collection time, and either enforce or soften the E5 no-hang guarantee
3. Re-run `dart test` on the five new test files — the suite should be green before re-review

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text
no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)
```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. This contradicts the PR's stated "degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as ask/request_secret".

Fix options: give `SessionSearchOutcome` a dedicated `unavailableReason` that the formatter prints verbatim, or return `truncated: true` here with the reason (the footer path already prints it). Add a tool-level test that runs the formatter against exactly this outcome.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text
no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)
```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. This contradicts the PR's stated "degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as ask/request_secret".

Fix options: give `SessionSearchOutcome` a dedicated `unavailableReason` that the formatter prints verbatim, or return `truncated: true` here with the reason (the footer path already prints it). Add a tool-level test that runs the formatter against exactly this outcome.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text
no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)
```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. This contradicts the PR's stated "degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as ask/request_secret".

Fix options: give `SessionSearchOutcome` a dedicated `unavailableReason` that the formatter prints verbatim, or return `truncated: true` here with the reason (the footer path already prints it). Add a tool-level test that runs the formatter against exactly this outcome.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment05.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the E5 "never a hang" guarantee is not enforceable — one record can blow the wall-clock budget**

The comment frames this cap as the E5 DoS bound, but a text-length cap is not a time bound on a backtracking regex engine (the Dart VM's `RegExp` backtracks — catastrophic patterns like `(a+)+$` over the 128 KB record are effectively unbounded). The time-budget check (`checkDeadline`) only runs **between** lines/blocks, never inside `pattern.hasMatch`, so a single pathological match on one giant record wedges the tool call — and the cancel token is not consulted during `execute` either — far beyond the promised 10 s, producing a hung agent rather than an "honest `truncated` report".

This matters more here than for a plain grep tool because the regex comes from the model itself, which routinely emits accidentally-quadratic patterns, and this PR's headline scenario is giant records.

Directions: bound the regex subject far smaller (a match over the first N KB of the record's preview-sized excerpt is enough for a pointer), or run the match in an isolate that can be abandoned on deadline expiry, or explicitly scope the E5 claim down to "budget checked between records" and cap per-record regex input accordingly.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment07.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: accumulator state grows linearly with archive size — the flat-memory claim (E4) does not hold**

`scanSessionSegment`'s doc claims "memory stays flat regardless of file size (E4)", and that is true only for the block/carry streaming. The accumulator itself retains per-record state for the whole chain: `_parentOf` for **every** record id (plus `_ordinalOf` in map mode, doubling it). For a multi-GB archive — this PR's explicit target — with a few million records this is hundreds of MB of id→parent pairs held for the entire scan, and it also accumulates identically on every continuation page.

Directions: the branch walk only needs parents of records on the leaf→root path. Since `RangedReadFileSystem` supports ranged reads, consider a two-pass approach (find the leaf in pass 1 storing only checkpoint/parent facts sparsely, then walk backwards in ranges), or keep parents only for records at/after the last observed fork, or correct the doc comment to state the linear bound honestly and decide whether it is acceptable for the E4 giant-session scenario.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the "no session file" degradation renders as "no records match" — the graceful-null contract is dishonest in practice**

When the host has no backing session file, this returns `truncated: false, truncationReason: 'no session file'` with zero totals. But `formatSessionSearchOutcome` only surfaces `truncationReason` when `truncated` is true, so the model actually sees:

```text
no records match (examined 0 of 0 records)
```

That claims the archive was scanned and is empty — the opposite of "this host cannot search". The tool-level null-callback branch (`'This host has no session file to search.'`) is never reached from the CLI because the callback is always `searchSessionArchive`. This contradicts the PR's stated "degrades to the same graceful cannot-execute result as ask/request_secret".

Fix options: give `SessionSearchOutcome` a dedicated `unavailableReason` that the formatter prints verbatim, or return `truncated: true` here with the reason (the footer path already prints it). Add a tool-level test that runs the formatter against exactly this outcome.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the hit cap is counted before the branch-scope filter — the default scope under-delivers and pages O(n²)**

`seeRecord` stops at `query.maxHits` hits in `_hits`, but `finish()` only then filters to the active branch. Since `branch` is the **default** scope, every match on an abandoned fork consumes budget and can trigger a premature `result cap` that returns far fewer than 40 branch hits — or zero — while reporting `truncated: true`. Worse, the continuation token skips records globally, so each next page re-scans the entire prefix of the chain: paging through a fork-heavy giant session is O(n²) under a 10 s budget.

No test covers branch-scope + cap together (the seeded fork record doesn't match the test query, so the E4 test can't see this).

Directions: collect hits with branch membership decided at collection time where possible, or over-collect with slack and continue scanning when the branch-filtered count is below the cap; alternatively exclude non-branch hits from the cap accounting and document that a capped branch scan may re-examine fork hits on the next page.
